meta.title: Hook verdict fidelity: published third-party guard inventory, with sandboxed byte captures and replay cells
meta.method: GitHub search through Firecrawl (research_search_github), then shallow clones (git clone --depth 1, repo hooks disabled) into separate directories; hook code and docs READ. Round 3: six guards' own hook entry points (four more could not be built offline) were then run inside sandbox-exec (deny default, no network, writes only under a scratch directory) on fixture payloads to capture their bytes (guard_capture.py), and the captured bytes were replayed through the Gemini hook runner (22 releases) and through Claude Code and Codex CLI against a local stub model (guard_replay.py). No paid API or real model was used.
meta.status_of_every_prediction: PREDICTED from vendor docs and Codex/Gemini source unless a row says MEASURED-RUNNER-LAYER (Gemini hook runner, no model), MEASURED-RUNNER-REPLAY, MEASURED-STUB-REPLAY (a harness CLI against the stub model) or MEASURED-CAPTURE (the guard's own bytes).
meta.selection_rule: Included if the repo ships a hook configuration for at least one of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini and its hook emits permissionDecision, a decision field, or exit 2 for a security purpose; ranked by the search tool, then cloned until the budget ended. The number of search hits rejected was not recorded.
meta.selection_caveat: Convenience sample from search ranking, not a census. Stars (repo-level, from the public GitHub API on 2026-11-01) and last-commit age are recorded per guard; install counts were not collected. Commits range from 2025-12 to 2026-10.

CC-FAILOPEN.statement: Empty stdout, malformed JSON, exit 1/3/126/127/other non-zero (except 2), missing or non-executable script, crash and timeout are all non-blocking: the tool call proceeds. `onFailure: block` (v2.1.295+) makes a failure act like exit 2; it is off by default.

CC-EXIT2.statement: Exit 2 blocks the call with stderr as the reason, before permission rules are evaluated.

CC-ASK-HEADLESS.statement: `ask` under `claude -p` (no human) is not stated for a hook ask. The hooks page says that when Claude Code denies a call in a -p run where no one can answer the prompt, Claude reads the reason in the tool result (indirect evidence for deny). The only measurement is a guard author's comment (cc-safe-setup, examples/memory-write-guard.sh, Claude Code 2.1.228): -p refuses the ask. Undocumented, and the only data point is a deny on one version.
CC-ASK-HEADLESS.basis: UNVERIFIED (undocumented; indirect DOC plus one third-party measurement pointing to deny)

CC-ASK-BYPASS.statement: `ask` under bypassPermissions / auto / dontAsk is not documented (bypass skips prompts except actions no mode auto-approves; the list names explicit ask rules, not hook asks). Public issue reports disagree by version.

CC-ALLOW-SCOPE.statement: Hook `allow` skips the prompt but deny/ask rules still apply, plus exceptions (network-path reads, requiresUserInteraction MCP tools, AskUserQuestion, critical-path rm, explicit ask rules).

CC-P-TRUST.statement: `-p` / SDK never shows the workspace-trust dialog and treats the folder as trusted, so repo hooks run in a never-trusted folder.

CC-MCP-RES.statement: ReadMcpResourceTool and ListMcpResourcesTool are built-in tools with built-in names; an `mcp__` matcher or `^mcp__` self-filter does not match them. No doc says so outright.
CC-MCP-RES.basis: DOC for ingredients; conclusion is an inference

CC-LEGACY-DECISION.statement: A top-level legacy `{decision: block}` on PreToolUse is deprecated but mapped: block becomes deny, approve becomes allow.
CC-LEGACY-DECISION.basis: DOC (hooks page, fetched 2026-11-01): the top-level decision/reason fields on PreToolUse are deprecated; the deprecated values approve and block map to allow and deny

CX-BLOCK-OK.statement: Blocking works for (a) PreToolUse JSON deny / decision:block with a non-empty reason and (b) exit 2 with non-empty stderr.

CX-ASK.statement: PreToolUse `ask` is parsed but unsupported: the hook run is marked Failed and the tool call CONTINUES.

CX-ALLOW.statement: `allow` without `updatedInput` is unsupported: hook Failed, call continues (same net effect as allow, plus an error).

CX-DENY-EMPTY.statement: `deny` with an empty reason is invalid: hook Failed, call continues.

CX-EXIT2-EMPTY.statement: Exit 2 with EMPTY stderr: hook Failed ("did not write a blocking reason"), call continues.

CX-EXIT-OTHER.statement: Exit 1, 126, 127, any other non-zero code, spawn error or no status code: hook Failed, call continues.
CX-EXIT-OTHER.basis: SRC; docs say only that a failure can fail the hook without blocking

CX-TIMEOUT.statement: Timeout (default 600 s): hook Failed, call continues.

CX-UNSUPPORTED-FIELDS.statement: `continue:false`, `stopReason`, `suppressOutput` are unsupported: hook Failed, call continues.

CX-MALFORMED.statement: Output that looks like JSON but does not parse: hook Failed, call continues.

CX-TRUST.statement: Non-managed user-config and hooks.json hooks must be reviewed and trusted; an untrusted one is not registered (skipped). Hooks delivered by a plugin follow plugin-level trust (discovery.rs registers a handler when `plugin_content_hash` is none and `plugin_trust` is some), so this row may not apply to them. The exposure is a fresh install or a changed hook before the first review, not a standing weakness. The startup warning in source is TUI-only; a headless warning is UNVERIFIED.

CX-COVERAGE.statement: PreToolUse covers Bash, apply_patch and MCP calls only; hosted tools (WebSearch) and some specialised paths do not use it. Docs: a useful guardrail, not a complete enforcement boundary. A public report says no hook fires for unified_exec/command_execution on some Desktop builds (not verified here).

CU-ASK-MCP.statement: `ask` for beforeMCPExecution is in the schema but reported not enforced when the MCP tool is allowlisted/approved: it ran 3/3 in an earlier live Cursor CLI run (not part of this task), matching IDE forum reports and one guard's source reading of the Cursor 3.24.18 executor.
CU-ASK-MCP.basis: FORUM + earlier measurement elsewhere; docs silent

CU-ASK-PRETOOLUSE.statement: `ask` on preToolUse is accepted by the schema but not enforced.

CU-ASK-SHELL.statement: `ask` on beforeShellExecution was held in the earlier CLI run even when allowlisted; one Nov 2025 IDE forum report says an allowlisted shell ask auto-runs.
CU-ASK-SHELL.basis: DOC (schema only) + FORUM; earlier measurement elsewhere

CU-FAILCLOSED.statement: Crash, timeout, non-zero exit other than 2, and empty output fail OPEN unless the hook sets `failClosed: true`. Invalid JSON or a schema mismatch on a permission hook blocks regardless of failClosed.

CU-MISSING.statement: Missing hook script / missing interpreter / exit 126 is not documented. Guess: it is the same as a non-zero exit (fails open without failClosed).

CU-ALLOW.statement: A hook `allow` does not override Cursor's own approval/allowlist (forum, IDE).

CU-IMPORT.statement: Claude-plugin hooks imported by Cursor are reported to run with failClosed:false, and bash/jq hooks that print nothing on allow count as hook failures.

GM-DENY-OK.statement: `decision: deny|block` on stdout (exit 0) blocks in every approval mode including yolo.

GM-ASK.statement: BeforeTool `ask` is undocumented. 0.66.0 headless yolo: no non-interactive branch, waits indefinitely. 0.37.1 shell tool drops the forced ask (runs). MCP tool on a trusted server or allowlisted: ask silently approved (source prediction, never run).

GM-EXIT2-EMPTY.statement: Exit 2 with NO stdout and NO stderr: no output, so the call is ALLOWED in every one of 22 releases (docs say exit 2 blocks). Exit 2 with JSON on stdout: the JSON decides from 0.30.0 on; earlier releases ignore it. Exit 2 with text on stderr denies.
GM-EXIT2-EMPTY.basis: MEASURED (runner layer, no model); contradicts the docs

GM-EXIT-TEXT.statement: Exit 126/127/3+ with text on stderr or stdout becomes a DENY (stderr is the reason) from gemini-cli-core 0.30.0 on; with empty output the call is allowed; 0.29.7 and earlier allow with a warning. Docs say "Other: warning, continue". MEASURED at the hook-runner layer on 22 releases (results/hook-fidelity/gemini-core); the scheduler was not run.
GM-EXIT-TEXT.basis: MEASURED (runner layer, no model); contradicts the docs

GM-TIMEOUT.statement: Timeout (default 60 s) or spawn error: no output, call ALLOWED in every release measured (1.5 s timeout tested; the 60 s default and a grandchild that holds the pipe are covered by the sweep's last scenarios).

GM-PLAINTEXT.statement: Plain-text stdout with exit 0 becomes allow plus a systemMessage; malformed JSON is treated as plain text (exit 1 allows with a warning).

CU-SDK-SHAPE.statement: A guard built on a polyhook SDK may not recognise a harness's event payload; the guard then answers `{}` and the call proceeds. Whether Cursor's real beforeShellExecution payload is recognised is not established.
CU-SDK-SHAPE.basis: MEASURED at the guard on one fixture shape; payload not recorded from a live Cursor

guards.own_error: No jq: core hooks print a once-per-session stderr warning that they are NOT protecting you, then allow (README: blocking every call would make Claude Code unusable). Example hooks without a fallback silently parse an empty command and exit 0. No `onFailure` setting found anywhere in the repo.

quotes.text: Only `exit 2` counts as blocked here; `exit 1`, `exit 127` and a crash all let the command run.
Without a JSON parser they print a warning to stderr and exit `0` — and Claude Code stops for exit code `2`, not for warnings.
an "ask" needs somebody present to answer, so for fully unattended runs use CC_MEMORY_WRITE_APPROVAL=block (exit 2), which is enforced regardless of permission mode.
Non-interactively (claude -p) the call is refused rather than approved. [guard author's own measurement on Claude Code 2.1.228; not ours]

guards.name: destructive_command_guard (dcg)
guards.found_by: GitHub search: Codex PreToolUse guard; issues #77, #183
guards.interpreter: Native Rust binary `dcg` on PATH for Claude, Codex and Gemini (a missing binary is exit 127). For Cursor the installer writes a python3 bridge (`~/.cursor/hooks/dcg-pre-shell.py`) that runs dcg: a missing python3 is the Cursor-side interpreter risk.

verdicts.emission: JSON hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision "deny" + extra fields (ruleId, allowOnceCode...), exit 0
minimal JSON {hookSpecificOutput:{permissionDecision:deny, reason}} only, exit 0 (src/hook.rs:4405: Codex does not support `ask`)

verdicts.situation: evaluation deadline expired / command over max_command_bytes
verdicts.emission: `ask` on review-capable protocols (Claude-compatible, Copilot); `deny` on Codex and other non-review clients; `unverified_decision="deny"` turns ask into deny; payload permission_mode bypassPermissions or dontAsk gets deny automatically

guards.own_error: Malformed or oversized raw hook JSON: allow with an audit warning (fail-open) unless general.fail_closed / DCG_FAIL_CLOSED=1. Transient stdin I/O error: always allow. Panic after config load: the unverified-command response (ask or deny). Parse/config/runtime error exit 1 or 2 (docs/codex-integration.md). Cursor bridge: denies in-process on crash, timeout, unreadable or empty payload, non-zero exit and no verdict (DCG_BRIDGE_CRASH_DECISION=allow turns that off); a missing or unrunnable dcg is allowed on purpose.

quotes.text: It never treats elapsed analysis time or an oversized extracted command as proof that execution is safe.

the default `ask` presumes a human is present to answer. On unattended or autonomous sessions there is no such human, and anything auto-answering prompts would approve exactly the commands dcg declined to inspect.
Claude Code documents that a hook `deny` holds in those modes, but not what a hook `ask` does there.
the legacy exit-2 path being classified as `PreToolUse Failed` and then failing open, whereas the minimal JSON denial blocks correctly (#183).
dcg behavior under this gap is **fail-open by construction**: when Codex routes a command through `unified_exec`/`command_execution`, *no* `PreToolUse` hook fires

gaps.claim_at_risk: default ask for unverified commands (timeout, oversize)
gaps.prediction: dcg only auto-denies for permission_mode bypassPermissions/dontAsk. Whether a -p payload reports another mode (e.g. default) is not checked here; if it does, the ask reaches a harness with no human and its outcome is undocumented (inferred deny). dcg's README states the human assumption.

guards.own_error: warn mode (default): provider errors and timeouts fail open. enforce mode: fail-closed. hooks.json sets failClosed:true on shell, MCP, read-file and preToolUse, false on beforeSubmitPrompt. Missing binary under a failClosed hook gives exit 127 and the guard says every agent tool is then locked.

quotes.text: for **autonomous/auto-run** agents prefer `warn`, because with no human present the dialog is auto-approved.
`enforce` (locked) is the actual security floor for a managed fleet: the only mode that *guarantees* a flagged action is blocked regardless of who is at the keyboard.
A fail-closed hook whose target binary doesn't exist locks every agent tool with `exit 127` until an operator fixes the manifest from outside the session.
